newsitem.title: USA: Cell Genesys in patent cross-license pact.
newsitem.headline: Cell Genesys in patent cross-license pact.

text.p: Cell Genesys Inc said it and Japan Tobacco Inc had entered into a patent cross-license and settlement agreement with GenPharm International for human monoclonal antibody technology.
The agreement resolves all related litigation and claims between the parties, Cell Genesys said.
The technology involves genetically modified strains of mice capable of producing human monoclonal antibodies for disease therapy, it said in a statement released Thursday.

In consideration of the cross-license and settlement agreement, Cell Genesys said it agreed to issue to GenPharm a note due Sept 30, 1998, for $15 million, which bears interest at 7.0 percent and is convertible at the option of GenPharm into 1.7 million shares of Cell Genesys at $9 per share. The conversion price is subject to reset in 12 months.
In addition, Japan Tobacco agreed to make a cash payment to GenPharm, Cell Genesys said. It did not specify the size of the payment.

The agreement also calls for two potential milestone payments of $7.5 million each to GenPharm based on the future issuance of certain patents relating to human monoclonal antibody technology in Europe, Japan and/or the United States. These payments will be made by Xenotech L.P., a joint venture of Japan Tobacco and Cell Genesys's Abgenix Inc subsidiary.
As part of the cross-license agreement, Cell Genesys said it was granted a worldwide non-exclusive license in the field of gene therapy to certain technology of GenPharm.

The agreement includes a worldwide royalty-free cross-license to all issued and related patent applications pertaining to the generation of fully human monoclonal antibodies in genetically modified strains of mice.
